decisions.summary: The transition map had no topological codomain because the GL supplier fixed only its algebraic set. The definition now gives M_n(F) its Euclidean topology and GL_n(F) the subspace topology, so continuity is typed.

The tubular datum now explicitly satisfies e∘s=i for the supplied embedding i:B→M. This makes the collapse the one associated with that embedded zero section rather than with an unrelated disk-bundle neighborhood.
The ambient F^{N+1} and finite-stage classifying map are now restricted to finite N. The N=∞ case is defined as the filtered union inside F^∞, where the classifying map is literally the identity.
The statement and Given block now fix F∈{R,C}, exactly the fields for which the stable frame, norm, orthogonal-block, and Gram-normalization argument is defined.

The proposition now fixes a commutative unital ring and restricts every bundle to the R-oriented numerable CW/CW-type scope of the invoked Thom and Gysin interfaces. The iterated tubular identification remains explicitly supplied.

F2 and Step 2.1 now cite lem-the-filtered-differential-induces-d-r-on-the-r-page, whose statement gives the exact local rule [x]↦[∂x]. This licenses the equality with the positive pair connector before the vertical-axis quotient.

Step 4 no longer extends a ring-coefficient local-system theorem to arbitrary abelian G. It compares the two lifted transport maps using lifting-function independence and applies the singular prism identity after tensoring with the given G.
Step 3.1 now separates reduced based products from absolute products. Absolute K^{-i}(X) uses Σ^iX_+, and X_+∧Y_+≅(X×Y)_+ gives the claimed target; relative products use quotient spaces.

The homological exact-couple dependency and fact were removed. Step 4 now obtains the long exact sequence directly by placing the consecutive two-row filtration short exact sequences together and using the kernel/cokernel formulas from the sole cohomological differential.

Step 3 now computes the Mayer–Vietoris connector square inside the termwise split small-cochain sequences: a lifted cocycle is cupped with the closed Thom cocycle, and the explicit Leibniz formula gives the lower connector up to the stated unit sign.

The twisted clause now uses only the relative-Serre E2 formula stated by F2, together with direct disk-pair and orientation-local-system suppliers. It no longer cites internal proof sentences of an oriented-only result.

The proof now shows the coproduct quotient map is open by writing each saturation piece as a union of images under overlap homeomorphisms. Its restriction over U_i is therefore quotient, and both p and Φ_i are continuous by the quotient universal property.

The pre-Bott theorem now claims exactly the sequence constructed by successive mapping cones: it continues indefinitely to the left through reduced suspensions. It expressly does not assert positive-degree/desuspension groups.

The item now distinguishes the UCT statement, which omits AC, from its directly cited cycle-and-boundary freeness dependency, which explicitly assumes AC. AC is retained and attributed only to that exact dependency, avoiding both the rejected misattribution and an unsupported choice-free strengthening.

The facts now directly cite the relative product definition and cup-product associativity. Step 4 identifies repeated Alexander–Whitney products at cochain level and then uses connector naturality to identify the ordered fiber factor with v_n.

Step 4 no longer applies a CW-pair product theorem to the mapping-path total space. CW skeletal inclusions are replaced by open NDR neighborhoods; their deformations lift through the Hurewicz fibration, so the open-triad relative product applies and transports back by relative homotopy invariance.
